R0007.title: Unauthorized Plugin Promotion
R0007.definition: Conducting promotions through plugin-type applications or plugins attached to application clients.
R0007.description: Unauthorized promotional plugins can be implemented in three modes: as an add-on attached to a browser or application client; by hijacking traffic on the access terminal and intercepting/redirecting specific traffic; or as a third-party tool or website (e.g., price comparison or cashback sites) conducting illegal promotions.
R0007.influence: Causes economic losses to the platform and customer attrition.

references.title: Rule Guide: Interpretation of Rules on "Unauthorized Plugin Promotion"

observables: Unauthorized platform-promotion plugins are distributed via browser extension stores or third-party channels
Client traffic shows plugin-injected promotional redirects or price-comparison overlay requests
Promotion attribution data contains large volumes of commission settlements from unknown plugin channels
The same plugin package signature or extension ID is tied to multiple unauthorized promotion behaviors

R0007-001.title: Third-Party Price Comparison
R0007-001.definition: While a user is browsing a normal product detail page, providing price comparisons for the same product from competing websites.
R0007-001.description: Typical unauthorized promotional plugins exist as browser extensions, as well as app add-on plugins. While reasonable price comparison benefits market activity and saves consumer spending, incomplete or intentionally biased comparisons can cause economic losses or customer attrition — for example, comparing different brands, different models, or different service tiers.
R0007-001.influence: Abuse of price transparency hijacks platform traffic to competitors; platform commissions and subsidies are siphoned off, accelerating customer attrition.

observables: Product detail pages are injected with a cross-site price-comparison overlay whose requests target a third-party price-comparison service domain
Competitor prices in the comparison data are selectively displayed, with an unreasonable comparison baseline
Users' browser extension lists contain price-comparison plugins not listed on the official store
The range of product data requested by the comparison plugin does not match the user's normal browsing trail

R0007-002.title: Access Link Hijacking
R0007-002.definition: Hijacking users' normal access requests and illegally redirecting them to other sites, cashback pages, or promotional pages.
R0007-002.description: Using viruses, trojans, malicious plugins, unauthorized bundled software, forced homepage setting, browser hijacking, page hijacking, search engine manipulation, or user information tampering to hijack normal traffic. Or during normal browsing, hijacking website traffic by modifying URL parameters or using pop-ups/floating windows.
R0007-002.influence: User access traffic is illegally hijacked and diverted; platform commissions and promotional resources are intercepted, normal promotion attribution is distorted, and customers are lost.

references.title: Software Extensions, Technique T1176 - MITRE ATT&CK

observables: User requests to the target domain are abnormally redirected to promotional or cashback pages
Browser address-bar URL parameters are tampered with by a plugin, injecting promotional tracking parameters
Non-platform-official pop-ups, overlays, or redirect scripts are injected during page loading
An unauthorized module in the client process hooks network requests and modifies the destination address

R0007-003.title: Unauthorized Promotional Redirection
R0007-003.definition: While a user is browsing a normal product detail page, providing information that induces the user to purchase from another page.
R0007-003.description: Typical unauthorized promotional plugins exist as browser extensions, as well as app add-on plugins. The main tactic is to present more attractive or better-value product information when a user views a product, or to guide users to download a client through cashback or commission-sharing schemes.
R0007-003.influence: Users are induced to transact off-site; platform orders and commissions are lost, and legitimate promotion channels are squeezed by unauthorized diversion.

references.title: Taobao Rules on Inducing Third-Party Transactions Implementation Rules - Alimama Headlines
Interim Provisions on Countering Unfair Competition in Cyberspace - gov.cn

observables: Product detail pages are injected with off-site purchase guidance whose links point to competitor or shopping-guide platforms
Cashback or commission-sharing lures appear on the page guiding users to download third-party clients
Promotional guidance content loads dynamically based on user access behavior, with origin domains not belonging to the platform
The user conversion funnel shows large volumes of churn nodes redirecting to external promotional links

R0007-004.title: Unauthorized Plugin Cashback
R0007-004.definition: While a user is browsing a normal product detail page, the plugin label displays cashback information for that product.
R0007-004.description: Typical cashback plugins exist as browser extensions, as well as app add-on plugins and third-party apps or websites. The main tactic is to obtain the affiliate commission for a product when a user views it, then share a portion of that commission back to the user as cashback.
R0007-004.influence: Cashback plugins hijack order attribution to siphon affiliate commissions; platform commissions are unlawfully shared out and legitimate affiliate channels suffer.

observables: Product detail pages are injected with cashback labels whose requests target third-party cashback services
Affiliate commission settlements contain attribution from unknown plugin channels, crowding out the official affiliate share
The user ordering flow is hijacked by a plugin that appends promotional tracking parameters to siphon commissions
The same cashback plugin is tied to commission-claim requests across many products, spiking during campaign periods
